question: After runtime's verified byte-preserving nginx HIT-cache substrate (oracle-free decompression 960/960 byte-identical across HIT/SWR/SIE/304 stages), does a controlled single-resource local perturbation (DOM attribute/text change, endpoint param/header change, Cache-Control/ETag mutation) require only localized repair — bounded tokens/browser/verification cost (<50% tokens and <40% browser vs cold re-exploration), verification AUROC>=0.75 and precision>=0.80, contamination <0.10 and amortized cost < cold at 10 reuses when measured with a real LLM agent, real Playwright execution and real verify() on actual DOM/response state?
hypothesis: C-DELTA-REPAIR hypothesis (real-substrate remeasurement): a single-resource local perturbation is repairable by a localized patch (re-target selector, rebind param slot, update header expectation, refresh cache key) without full-task re-exploration when measured with a real LLM, real Playwright, and real verify() on actual nginx+Flask state. Operational predictions on held-out TEST: (1) localized repair succeeds on >=80% pooled and >=70% per-family; (2) mean repair tokens <0.50 * mean B-COLD tokens AND mean browser interactions <0.40 * B-COLD AND mean verification steps <=2; (3) verification discriminates correct vs incorrect patch with AUROC >=0.75 and precision >=0.80 at TRAIN-calibrated operating threshold; (4) contamination of unrelated mechanisms <0.10; (5) amortized cost (repair + verification + 10*retrieval_cost) < B-COLD cost at n_reuses=10. Byte-preserving HIT-cache substrate guarantees decompressed body SHA256 identity across HIT/SWR/SIE/304 is >=0.99 pre-perturbation via oracle-free gzip.decompress, so post-perturbation divergence is attributable to the controlled local change, not decompression artefacts.
falsifier: C-DELTA-REPAIR is falsified (in this single-resource localhost setting) if ANY primary locality condition fails while measurement-validity gates pass: (F1) repair success <0.80 pooled OR <0.70 in any family on TEST; (F2) mean repair tokens >=0.50 * B-COLD tokens OR mean browser >=0.40 * B-COLD OR mean verification steps >2 on TEST; (F3) contamination >=0.10; (F4) verification AUROC <0.75 OR precision <0.80 at operating threshold on TEST; (F5) amortized repair at n_reuses=10 not cheaper than B-COLD (tokens or browser) on TEST. Global falsification requires failure across all three families; family-specific failure (e.g., DOM passes, ENDPOINT fails) yields MIXED with per-family ceilings and does not falsify the entire claim. Measurement failure (C1-C3) yields MEASUREMENT_INVALID, not falsification.

baselines.description: Full cold re-exploration: same real LLM agent (same model id, temperature, max_tokens, tools, budget) solves the task from scratch with empty registry and no prior trajectory, executed via Playwright on localhost. Measures full task cost in tokens (prompt+completion), browser interactions, verification calls, latency. This is the cost delta-repair must amortize against.
baselines.expected: Succeeds on >=90% tasks but at full cost (100%). Repair must be <50% tokens and <40% browser steps on TEST to claim locality.

baselines.description: Verbatim mechanism replay without repair: stored mechanism from pre-perturbation executed unchanged on post-perturbation target via Playwright, no LLM patch. Strong 0-token replay baseline.
baselines.expected: Near 0% success post-perturbation (correctly fails). Demonstrates perturbation is breaking and repair adds value beyond trivial reuse. If replay succeeds >10%, perturbation was non-breaking and instance is excluded as non-discriminating.

baselines.description: Semantic retrieval over prior trajectory memory (embedding search + nearest successful trajectory replay) without patch, executed via Playwright. Represents strong retrieval baseline Graph must beat to justify repair mechanics over RAG.
baselines.expected: Partial success 20-40%. Repair should exceed retrieval by >=30pp success on TEST.

baselines.description: Oracle hand-authored minimal patch (single selector/param/header correction) applied by experimenter, executed and verified via Playwright. Upper-bound ceiling for achievable localized repair.
baselines.expected: 100% success with 1 browser probe + 1 verification. Provides cost ceiling; measured autonomous repair should approach oracle within 2x tokens/steps to be considered near-optimal, but ceiling alone does not confirm hypothesis.

baselines.description: Runtime verified substrate invariant: oracle-free decompression (gzip.decompress without oracle lookup, handling Content-Encoding, chunked, Vary) yields byte-identical decompressed bodies across HIT, SWR (stale-while-revalidate), SIE (stale-if-error), and 304 Not Modified stages on unperturbed resources, on real nginx 1.2x reverse-proxy + Flask 3.1.3 + PyJWT HS256.
baselines.expected: >=0.99 SHA256(body) identity HIT==SWR==SIE==304 pre-perturbation (960/960 equivalent scaled to instance count). If this baseline drifts <0.99, measurement is invalid per C-MEAS-VALID.

positive_control.description: Two positive controls executed via identical real LLM+Playwright+verify pipeline: (PC1) Unperturbed execution: mechanism resolved and verified on pre-perturbation endpoint with no patch succeeds and verify()=true, byte identity holds. (PC2) Known-break single-attribute perturbation with oracle patch: Flask+nginx testbed where target DOM id changes #submit-123->#submit-124 (or param ?id=->?item=) and oracle patch updates selector/param; repair succeeds within 2 browser probes and verification passes, cost ratio <0.5 vs B-COLD. Both use real tokens, real browser counts, real verify() on actual DOM/response.
positive_control.expected: PC1 100% success (Wilson CI reported), PC2 >=90% success with token ratio <0.5 vs B-COLD. If either fails, instrumentation is broken, not the hypothesis — triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

null_control.description: Two null controls via real pipeline: (NC1) Zero perturbation (identical pre/post resource): proposed repair pipeline must produce zero patch (repair tokens ~0 aside from 1 verification probe, contamination 0, verify no false patch) and byte identity 1.0 across all cache stages. (NC2) Distant unrelated perturbation (modify endpoint B while target is endpoint A): repair of A must be no-op, success on A unchanged, contamination on B-independent mechanisms remains 0. Both tested with permutation-shuffled random-patch decisions to verify false-accept detection. Real verify() scores used for AUROC baseline.
null_control.expected: NC1 repair cost = 0 patch tokens, NC1 contamination =0, NC2 contamination =0, random-patch false-accept <=5% and AUROC ~0.5 (0.4-0.6). If NC fails, pipeline is mis-calibrated — triggers MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

measurement_validity: Substrate provenance (real, not simulated): nginx 1.2x reverse-proxy with HIT/SWR/SIE/304 caching (Cache-Control max-age, stale-while-revalidate, stale-if-error), Flask 3.1.3 backend with PyJWT HS256 HS256 auth, SQLite fixture, Content-Encoding gzip where applicable, oracle-free decompression path (gzip.decompress on raw bytes without oracle lookup). Record nginx.conf hash, Flask testbed_server.py commit, decompression code hash, nginx --version, Python version, Playwright version. Verify >=0.99 byte-identical decompressed bodies pre-perturbation (SHA256(decompressed_body) HIT==SWR==SIE==304) on real nginx responses; recompute per instance pre and post.

Perturbation isolation (single-resource, real DOM/response): each instance mutates exactly one local resource — one DOM node attribute (id/class/data-testid) OR one text node OR one endpoint query param/header name OR one response header (Cache-Control max-age value, ETag value). No global config, no auth migration, no multi-resource drift. Perturbation manifest records file, line, old_value, new_value, blast_radius=1, and is held out from repair agent. Mutations applied to real Flask templates/static and nginx cache keys, observed via Playwright accessibility tree and real HTTP fetches. Cross-condition contamination checked by re-reading unrelated resources via Playwright+fetch.

Pre/post registry snapshot isolation: registry cloned before perturbation (deep copy with isolated storage); repair operates on clone; contamination measured as delta on uninvolved mechanism set (N>=24 unrelated mechanisms from distinct intents/endpoints) using real verify() on actual post-repair state. No leakage of perturbation manifest old->new mapping into repair prompt; repair agent sees only pre-perturbation mechanism + post-perturbation page/response observation (Playwright DOM snapshot + response headers/body) + verify() signal (pass/fail).

Cost measurement transparency (real, not simulated): tokens = sum(prompt_tokens + completion_tokens) from real LLM API responses (record model id, temperature, max_tokens, provider, per-call token counts); browser interactions = count(Playwright actions actually executed: goto, click, fill, evaluate, network fetch) with trace logs; verification cost = count(verify() + registry lookup + HIT-cache fetch) actually executed; wall-time measured. Full re-exploration cost measured with identical model/tools/budget and real execution. Retrieval cost included in amortized calculation via real embedding+retrieval timing. No hardcoded constants (prior COLD_TOKENS_BASE 2250, ORACLE_TOKENS 120, retrieval 320 removed); all costs are measured.

Verification validity (real postconditions, not deterministic scores): verify(mechanism_id, observed_state) checks postconditions on actual response/DOM state (DOM selector existence via Playwright evaluate, response status/header/body match), not on expected label. False accepts measured as verify()=true but observed_state functionally wrong (checked by independent oracle script using ground-truth selector/param/header from manifest, not available to repair agent). Threshold calibration: verification operating threshold (score cut at 0.6 or learned) fit on TRAIN perturbations only (18-36 instances), evaluated on held-out TEST; post-state never leaks into pre-state features. Scores are real verify() confidences, not deterministic instance_id-derived perfect-separation scores. AUROC/precision computed on real TEST scores.

Adequacy and power: >=48 perturbation instances total (3 families x 2 variants x 8 seeds =48) with family-stratified TRAIN/TEST split (24 TRAIN, 24 TEST), yielding per-family TEST n=8 and pooled TEST n=24. Each family has independent success/cost reported; pooled primary but per-family gates required. If any family TEST n<8 or total n<48, mark as underpowered and primary per-family gate is exploratory (MIXED ceiling only). Pooled Wilson CI half-width at p=0.8 n=24 is +-0.14; per-family n=8 half-width +-0.26 (flagged as exploratory). Upgrade to 72 instances (12 per-family TEST) if compute budget allows, but 48 is minimum for powered pooled decision with per-family exploratory. If n<24 pooled TEST, MEASUREMENT_INVALID. 95% Wilson CIs for rates, bootstrap by instance (2000 resamples) for cost ratios.

Determinism and reproducibility: fixed seeds for perturbation generation, nginx cache key generation, and LLM repair (temperature 0.0, seed where supported); all hashes use hashlib.sha256, never Python hash(); record all commits (graph/delta_repair code, runtime fixture), seeds manifest, model ids, nginx/Playwright versions. Exclude flaky network/external sites — localhost nginx+Flask only. Retry once on 5xx unrelated to perturbation or Playwright timeout >10s; if persistent infrastructure failure, log and mark instance as infrastructure-excluded (not as repair failure), and require n still >=48 else MEASUREMENT_INVALID.

Byte-identity recomputation (real): for each instance, store SHA256(decompressed_body) for HIT, SWR, SIE, 304 pre and post via real nginx fetches with oracle-free decompression; post-perturbation HIT body for perturbed resource must differ from pre (mutation detected) while unperturbed resources remain >=0.99-equivalent. Decompression code path preserved from runtime fixture and hashed; any Content-Encoding/chunked/Vary handling divergence is logged as substrate drift.

Representation fidelity: raw observables preserved — full DOM snapshot + accessibility tree subset + response headers + decompressed body bytes + cache status header. No hash-only surrogate. Repair LLM is a real model (e.g., gpt-4o-mini or equivalent, recorded id), not a heuristic; browser interactions are Playwright-executed, not counted simulation. Audit required_fixes 1-5 explicitly addressed: real LLM, real Playwright, real verify(), real contamination, real nginx.
decision_rule: All thresholds applied on frozen pre-registered TEST data only (TRAIN used solely for verification threshold calibration). Compute per-instance metrics then aggregate on TEST. Gates: (C1) PC1 success=1.0 and PC2 repair success >=0.90 on real pipeline; else MEASUREMENT_INVALID. (C2) NC1 patch cost 0 (no spurious patch) and NC2 contamination=0 and random-patch false-accept <=5% with AUROC 0.4-0.6; else MEASUREMENT_INVALID (pipeline mis-calibrated). (C3) B-RUNTIME-BYTE-IDENTITY pre-perturbation byte identity >=0.99 on real nginx; else MEASUREMENT_INVALID. Primary gates (require ALL to CONFIRM localized repair on TEST): (C4) repair success rate >=0.80 pooled AND >=0.70 per family on TEST (Wilson CI reported); (C5) mean repair tokens <0.50 * mean B-COLD tokens AND mean browser interactions <0.40 * B-COLD AND mean verification steps <=2 on TEST (bootstrap 95% CI for ratios); (C6) contamination <0.10 (fraction unrelated mechanisms invalidated or false-accept) on TEST; (C7) verification AUROC >=0.75 and precision at operating threshold >=0.80 on TEST (threshold from TRAIN); (C8) amortized cost at n_reuses=10 (repair + verification + 10*retrieval_cost) < B-COLD cost (both tokens and browser) on TEST means. CONFIRMED if C1-C8 all PASS. FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING if any of C4-C8 fails while C1-C3 PASS (valid negative, cost-bounded locality fails even under minimal perturbations). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if any of C1-C3 fails or pooled TEST n<24 or substrate byte identity fails. MIXED if family-heterogeneous: >=1 family passes C4-C8 while another fails — report per-family ceilings and do not claim pooled confirmation. Effect sizes, 95% Wilson CIs for rates, bootstrap CIs for cost ratios, and per-family breakdown required. This decision_rule preserves stable metric/control identifiers M-repair_success_rate, M-repair_tokens_ratio_vs_cold, M-browser_ratio_vs_cold, M-verification_auroc, M-contamination_rate, M-amortized_cost_tokens_10, B-COLD-FULL-REEXPLORATION, PC-LOCALIZED-REPAIR-SUCCEEDS, NC-ZERO-AND-DISTANT-PERTURBATION.
product_consequence_positive: If CONFIRMED (C1-C8 PASS on real LLM+Playwright+verify), C-DELTA-REPAIR advances from HYPOTHESIS to EXPERIMENTAL (VALIDATED candidate pending replication) for single-resource local perturbations on real nginx HIT-cache localhost substrate. Justifies product architecture with localized repair boundaries: registry patch + verify loop rather than full task replay, with amortized cost advantage after 10 reuses. Next steps: expand perturbation radius (2-3 resources, cross-page), test on distributed Redis session store and production CDN, and integrate repair into SpiderKernel.invalidate()+distill() pipeline with freshness guard. Promotion to Product Core NOT authorized on localhost single-resource alone — requires cross-page and distributed validation.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (any C4-C8 fails while C1-C3 PASS on real measurement), single-resource locality fails even under minimal perturbations with real LLM/Playwright/verify, closing the smallest repair hypothesis. Product must default to full re-exploration or fused RAG+re-exploration for any drift, and must budget repair as equivalent to cold cost. Delta-repair claim remains HYPOTHESIS/BLOCKED for broader radius; Graph lane should pivot to C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY with matched families or C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE with calibrated abstention, both of which do not assume cheap local patches. Runtime HIT-cache substrate remains validated for measurement but not sufficient for repair. A valid negative prevents shipping a repair layer that would cause contamination/false accepts and is high information for allocation.
estimated_cost: Medium: reuse runtime nginx+Flask HS256 fixture (0.5h setup, real nginx 1.2x), generate 48 perturbation instances (1h, real templates), run B-COLD with real LLM+Playwright (48 instances * ~2k tokens ~96k tokens, 1.5h), run repair+verify loop per instance with real LLM (48 * ~1.5k tokens ~72k tokens, 1.5h), run retrieval RAG and verbatim baselines (0.5h), compute byte identity + contamination via real fetches (0.5h), analysis with Wilson/bootstrap (0.5h). Total ~6 compute-hours, ~170k tokens single LLM model, all localhost, no external sites beyond model API.
expected_information_gain: Very high: first ever real measurement of C-DELTA-REPAIR (0/224 canonical experiments valid; prior 1 was MEASUREMENT_INVALID simulation with hardcoded parameters that falsified C5/C8 as parameter artifacts). Directly tests SPIDER's core product promise 'pay novelty not whole task' with strong 0-token replay baseline, contamination and amortization economics, and verified byte-preserving substrate dependency. Either CONFIRMED (justifies repair architecture, unblocks residual-novelty amortization) or FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (closes cheapest repair hypothesis, prevents premature promotion, redirects Graph/Runtime/Product) materially changes claim state and next allocation for graph/runtime/product. Advances beyond saturated FRESHNESS tunnel (14 recent, r~0.002-0.046, TOST PASS at delta=0.15) per Director PIVOT cognitive_reset rationale; cross-lane unblocking per unit effort highest among alternatives (C-PARAM-INHERIT starved, C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY needs this gate first).
